matching: A must_find entry is matched by a finding whose location is any file in `locations` and whose cited principle is any name in `principles`; `detail` disambiguates when one file carries more than one seed. A must_not_flag entry is violated by any finding targeting the construct described in `detail` at a file in `locations`. An allowed_extras entry excuses a finding at its location/detail from counting against precision.

must_find.detail: TableName.parse signals malformed user-reachable input with an undeclared IllegalArgumentException
SizeEstimator.estimate wraps the same-module SizeParser call in catch (RuntimeException) and returns a sentinel
vendor S3Exception (and decode failures) escape raw through the core-owned TableStore interface
principles: Failures flow low to high, translated once per boundary

must_find.detail: ErrorCodes is a shared error-code type crossing module boundaries
principles: Failures flow low to high, translated once per boundary

must_find.detail: SizeEstimator.readManifests performs file IO inside a stream lambda, wrapping IOException to get through map()
S3TableStore.load converts S3TimeoutException into Optional.empty(), surfacing an infrastructure failure as the domain outcome 'absent'
principles: Dependency failure is its own category

must_not_flag.detail: the TableDto/Table near-duplication and its mapper must not draw a consolidation recommendation
the catch (Exception) in RequestHandler.handle must not be flagged as an overly broad catch; it is a genuine entry point (findings about what the handler renders are separate and allowed)
the NumberFormatException catch in parseLimit is a correct JDK parse seam and must not be flagged
no finding may demand that an error surface conform to the triage vocabulary

allowed_extras.detail: an unparseable limit is rendered with the CONFLICT error code, erasing the invalid-input distinction
the entry-point catch renders every unmapped failure as STORAGE_DOWN, asserting a specific cause it does not know
the failure log records only the exception's toString and no identifying request context
decode's Long.parseLong lets a corrupt blob surface as NumberFormatException; often reported as part of vendor-exception-through-port
